nodes.summary: Let $G$ be the group with generators $a, b$ and the single defining relation $[[a, b], b] = 1$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$. Then $G$ is linear: there are a field $K$, a natural number $n$ and an injective group homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$.
nodes.title: The one-relator group of Kourovka Problem 18.86 is linear

nodes.summary: The statement that the group $G$ with generators $a, b$ and the single defining relation $[[a, b], b] = 1$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$, is linear: there are a field $K$, a natural number $n$ and an injective group homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.86 (statement)

nodes.summary: This is the group $G = \langle a, b \mid [[a, b], b] = 1 \rangle$ with generators $a, b$ and the single defining relation $[[a, b], b] = 1$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$; that is, $G$ is the quotient of the free group on $a$ and $b$ by the normal subgroup generated by $[[a, b], b]$.
nodes.title: The one-relator group of Kourovka Problem 18.86

nodes.summary: This is the element $[[a, b], b]$ of the free group on two generators $a$ and $b$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$; explicitly, $[[a, b], b] = c^{-1} b^{-1} c b$ with $c = a^{-1} b^{-1} a b$.
nodes.title: The relator of Kourovka Problem 18.86
